purpose: Defects M00 confirmed and reproduced, each with a test that runs on every build. An open defect is characterised by a test asserting the CURRENT, broken behaviour; a fixed defect keeps the same test asserting the fix, so the defect cannot quietly come back. Fixing one without updating this file makes the corresponding test fail, which is the point: the fix has to be a deliberate act, not a drift nobody notices.
note: Read the entry's status and owner fields before changing a test. A failing test here means one of three things, and the failure message says which: the phase named in owner has landed and this registry needs updating, a fixed defect has regressed, or an untouched defect changed behaviour.
statusVocabulary: open - the defect is present; its test asserts the broken behaviour and fails when the defect is fixed
fixed - the defect is gone; its test asserts the correct behaviour and fails if the defect returns
partially fixed - the specified half is fixed and the rest is owned by another phase; the entry says which half

defects.title: FailureCode.RESOLVER_INIT_FAILED is declared, translated for the user, and unreachable
defects.fixedIn: the resolver-init branch of FailureCode.classify, matching the engine's own name in the stage hint or the throwable message
defects.current_behaviour: FailureCode.classify() returns CLASS_NOT_FOUND, MEMBER_NOT_FOUND, ACCESS_DENIED, TIMEOUT, RESOLVER_AMBIGUOUS or UNEXPECTED. It has no branch returning RESOLVER_INIT_FAILED, and no production code constructs a report with that code.
defects.symptom: The one failure mode the code was written for - the module could not initialise DexKit - is never reported. UserExplanation has a sentence for it that can never be shown.
defects.root_cause: FeatureLoader.start() runs before Instrumentation.callApplicationOnCreate, so FailureReportStore has no Application to attach to. The failure is logged to the Xposed log and start() returns with zero hooks installed.
defects.fixedWording: The test now asserts the fix from both sides: the function must contain a path that returns RESOLVER_INIT_FAILED, and one concrete DexKit-style failure must classify as it, while a failure that names neither the engine nor the stage still reports UNEXPECTED rather than being attributed to the engine.

defects.title: A DexKit initialisation failure stopped the whole bootstrap and reported nothing
defects.fixedIn: the declared stage sequence in com.wax.module.bootstrap: fourteen ordered stages, each with a criticality and a dependency set, run by StageRunner in two passes. The engine is one stage rather than a guard in the middle of start(), so its failure skips the six stages that need it, names the engine as the cause, and leaves the five that do not standing
defects.current_behaviour: There is no early return after the engine failure. FeatureLoader.start runs a StageRunner sequence: once before the target Application exists and once after it does. The engine is the DEX_ENGINE stage; when it fails, RESOLVER_CACHE, CORE, ESSENTIAL, OPTIONAL, RUNTIME_VERIFICATION and READY are recorded as SKIPPED with DEX_ENGINE named as the cause, and FRAMEWORK, MODULE, SCOPE, TARGET, INJECTION, PREFERENCES and APPLICATION_ATTACH still ran.
defects.symptom: Resolved. The engine failure is recorded before it happens, is classified as the engine, is visible to the Manager on the next heartbeat, and no longer decides the fate of the stages that never needed the engine.
defects.root_cause: Fixed by making the sequence a declared one. A guard in the middle of a method cannot say which later work needed the thing it guarded, so it can only stop all of it - and a stage that was never reached could not report that it was never reached.
defects.gate: M03 Gate: a DexKit failure is diagnosable, an optional failure cannot block READY, and the bootstrap is deterministic and idempotent. StageRunnerTest asserts each clause.
defects.fixedWording: The test now asserts the fix from both sides: the guard still exists and the failure is still recorded with the stage named, and there is no return after it any more - re-adding one would stop every later stage again, including the ones that never needed the engine. The health reporter is still created before the sequence runs, which is the ordering M00 identified as the root cause.

defects.title: The status banner is the module's opinion of itself, not the runtime's state
defects.fixedIn: the activation model in com.wax.module.activation: a per-target heartbeat produced by the runtime from inside the target process, an ActivationSignal hierarchy in which the self-hook is the weakest source, one ActivationState per distinguishable situation, and a resolver that refuses to infer a scope or module failure from absence
defects.current_behaviour: isLegacySelfHookSignal() is still System.currentTimeMillis() == 0L and is still installed by the self-hook, but it is no longer the activation signal. It is ActivationSignal.LEGACY_SELF_HOOK_SIGNAL, ranked below the framework evidence a target reports about itself, and the Home screen renders a state resolved from that heartbeat rather than from this boolean.
defects.symptom: Resolved. The banner no longer claims a module is active for the reason that it is running. Each card names one of: not installed, not running, running but not injected, bootstrapping, degraded, failed, ready, or nothing reported - and the failure that produced the state travels with it.
defects.root_cause: Fixed by separating the question from its source. A self-hook can answer "did a framework load WA X somewhere" and nothing else, and no other claim may be derived from it.
defects.gate: Gate A of #321. A generic activation message is permitted for exactly one failure code - INJECTION_NOT_OBSERVED, which requires a framework to be proven present and a target process to be proven alive - and for no other. SCOPE_MISSING and MODULE_DISABLED cannot be proven from a third process and are never produced there.
defects.fixedWording: Both original tests now assert the fix from the other side: the placeholder is named for the signal it carries rather than for the question it was asked, and the hook that installs it is still reachable only for the module's own package. A third test asserts that no screen can fall back on a generic activation message, because the message being gone is what makes the fix structural rather than cosmetic.

defects.title: modulePath is passed to XModuleResources.createInstance without a null guard
defects.current_behaviour: modulePath is String? and assigned only in initZygote. createInstance's first parameter is a Java platform type, so Kotlin accepts passing null when initZygote has not run.
defects.symptom: Resource injection is handed a null module path. The failure mode is not asserted here because it depends on LSPosed callback ordering that cannot be reproduced off-device.
defects.root_cause: A nullable field is consumed by a platform-typed Java call with no guard.

defects.title: Resource injection swallows every exception, so it fails silently
defects.current_behaviour: The loop that walks R.array, R.string and R.drawable and rewrites their static int fields is wrapped in catch (_: Exception) {} with an empty body.
defects.symptom: A failed injection means WA X's resources silently do not apply while the banner reads "enabled".
defects.root_cause: An empty catch turns a real failure into a missing feature. Counted under silent_catch in the M00.06 inventory.
